title: Deterministic Bounds on Accuracy and Stability of Metric-Space Regression and Classification
abstract: arXiv:2610.22564v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Data-driven approaches often face ambiguity in datasets due to sensor or target noise, insufficient information, and noise in the input data. While best-fit machine learning methods can accommodate such noise through uncertainty estimates, they are prone to overfitting and it is challenging to quantify ambiguity of the relation between inputs and targets. We introduce a geometric framework that quantifies this ambiguity through the average kernel size, computed with data-dependent, i.e. model-independent, feasible sets derived from worst-case input and target noise. The framework provides computable, deterministic, non-asymptotic bounds on the best achievable empirical error and accuracy for a finite, constructed dataset, independent of the predictive model class, and applies to regression and classification with pseudo-metric input spaces and metric target spaces. translated_title: 度量空间回归与分类的精度与稳定性的确定性界限
translated_abstract: 数据驱动方法常常由于传感器或目标噪声、信息不足以及输入数据中的噪声而面临数据集中的模糊性问题。虽然最优拟合机器学习方法可以通过不确定性估计来容纳这种噪声，但它们容易过拟合，且难以量化输入与目标之间关系的模糊性。我们引入了一个几何框架，通过平均核大小来量化这种模糊性，该框架使用基于数据的（即与模型无关的）可行集进行计算，这些可行集由最坏情况下的输入和目标噪声导出。该框架为有限构建数据集上可实现的最低经验误差和最高精度提供了可计算的、确定性的、非渐近的界限，且与预测模型类无关，适用于具有伪度量输入空间和度量目标空间的回归与分类问题。输入-目标关系的模糊性意味着三个后果：……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一个几何框架，通过基于最坏情况输入和目标噪声计算的平均核大小，为度量空间回归和分类任务提供了与模型无关的、可计算的确定性精度与误差界限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a geometric framework that quantifies input-target ambiguity through average kernel size, providing computable, deterministic, non-asymptotic, model-independent bounds on achievable accuracy and empirical error for metric-space regression and classification.
